name: MUN negotiation
notes: Criteria carried over from the v2 rubric (shared/rubric.js). Scored by staff. The old keyword scorer survives only as optional checklist hints (D-010).

criteria.name: Protocol and register
criteria.hint: Third person, formal address to the chair or committee.
levels: Mostly informal with some formal phrases.
Third person throughout; little formal address.
Third person, formal address, occasional slips.
Consistently formal and diplomatic; addresses the chair and committee correctly.

criteria.name: National interest
criteria.hint: Connects the position to the country's real situation.
levels: No link to the country's situation.
Names the country but not its interests.
Explains an interest with one concrete fact.
Builds the position from the country's interests with specific, sourced facts.

criteria.name: Specificity
criteria.hint: Refers to particular paragraphs, figures or mechanisms.
levels: Refers to a paragraph or figure.
Refers precisely to text and numbers.
Precise references that drive the argument (paragraph, wording, figures).

criteria.name: Engagement
criteria.hint: Responds to what other delegates actually said.
levels: Responds directly and accurately to others' points.
Shapes the debate by answering, linking and building on others' points.

criteria.name: Trade and compromise
criteria.hint: Makes a conditional offer or proposes compromise wording.
levels: A clear conditional offer tied to specific wording.
A credible deal: what is offered, what is asked, and the wording that would secure it.

criteria.name: Concision
criteria.hint: Says it clearly within the time.
levels: Hard to follow or far over time.

name: Debating speaker (matter, manner, method)
notes: Assumed common Australian schools scale: matter 40, manner 40, method 20 (total 100). Check against the competition's rules and edit as needed.

criteria.name: Matter
criteria.hint: Arguments, examples and rebuttal: what was said.
levels: Relevant arguments with examples; some rebuttal.
Well-supported arguments; rebuttal engages the other side's best points.
Compelling, well-chosen arguments and incisive rebuttal.

criteria.name: Manner
criteria.hint: Delivery: voice, eye contact, presence, persuasion.

criteria.name: Method
criteria.hint: Structure, role fulfilment, timing, teamwork.
levels: Signposted structure; role done well; good timing.
Structure and teamwork make the case easy to follow.

name: Solo speech practice
notes: For solo practice and self-review. A student rates their own speech; staff can add a rating.

criteria.name: Content
criteria.hint: Clear point, reasons and examples.
levels: A point with reasons and a good example.
A memorable point, well reasoned and illustrated.

criteria.name: Structure
criteria.hint: Opening, body and conclusion.
levels: Opening, body and end are visible.
Structure makes the speech feel effortless.

criteria.name: Delivery
criteria.hint: Voice, pace, eye contact.
levels: Varied voice and pace for effect.

criteria.name: Time management
criteria.hint: Uses the time well.

name: Adjudicator feedback (from teams)
notes: Optional. Teams rate the adjudication they received. Used to support adjudicator development, not to grade staff.

criteria.name: Clear reasoning
criteria.hint: Was the decision explained?
levels: Clear reasons linked to the debate.
Clear, specific reasons that both teams could follow.

criteria.name: Helpful feedback
criteria.hint: Could the team act on it?
levels: Specific, actionable feedback for each speaker.

name: Written argument
notes: Prep studio (D-076): quality of one written argument. The structure check (which parts are written) is counted separately.

criteria.name: Clarity
criteria.hint: Is the claim one clear sentence a listener could repeat?
levels: A claim, but vague or too broad.
A clear, specific claim that fits the team line.
A sharp claim that is easy to remember and repeat.

criteria.name: Reasoning
criteria.hint: Does each step of the logic follow from the last?
levels: Logical steps that explain why it's true.
Tight logic that answers the obvious objections.

criteria.name: Example or evidence
criteria.hint: Is there a real, relevant example?
levels: Well-chosen examples that prove the point.

criteria.name: Impact and relevance
criteria.hint: Does it show why the point matters and how it proves the motion?
levels: Shows why it matters and to whom.
Shows why this point wins the debate.

name: Written rebuttal
notes: Prep studio (D-076): quality of one written rebuttal (they say, but, because, so).

criteria.name: Fair summary
criteria.hint: Is their argument summarised fairly, at its strongest?
levels: Their argument is missing or misstated.
A weak version of their argument.
A fair summary of their best version.
Their best version, put better than they might.

criteria.name: Clash
criteria.hint: Does it show exactly what's wrong: a flaw, a missing step or a false assumption?
levels: Says it's wrong but not why.
Takes the argument apart at its weakest point.

criteria.name: Support
criteria.hint: Is the answer backed by a reason or an example?
levels: A reason and a good example.
Support that the other side will find hard to answer.

criteria.name: Weighing
criteria.hint: Does it say why winning this point matters for the debate?
levels: No link back to the debate.
Shows why this clash decides the debate.
